name: Indie twang / yallternative
definition: Loud, loose guitar rock with pedal steel and country phrasing, made by punk- and indie-raised bands in the 2010s–2020s; Crazy Horse tone, small-town detail, deadpan or drawled vocals.

name: Barroom storytellers and deadpan songwriters
definition: Wordy, funny-sad songwriting in the John Prine / David Berman line: half-spoken vocals, long verses, jokes that turn into grief, bar-band or home-studio backing.

name: New alt-country and honky-tonk bands
definition: 2010s–2020s bands and songwriters playing recognizable country (honky-tonk, '90s country, bluegrass-inflected) with indie-scene provenance, labels, and audiences.

name: Countrygaze and loud twang
definition: Shoegaze- and noise-rock-scale guitar walls under pedal steel, twang, and country-song structures; the Wednesday template.

name: Twangy indie folk
definition: Hushed or fervent acoustic-led songwriting with fiddle, pedal steel, and open tunings, from Big Thief's circle outward; folk lineage from Townes and Gillian Welch through the 2010s Bandcamp scene.

name: Cosmic country and the '70s revival
definition: Grateful Dead-, Gram Parsons- and Laurel Canyon-indebted guitar bands and songwriters: buttery lead guitar, harmonies, breezy tempos, long instrumental passages.

name: Slacker, jangle, and power-pop revival
definition: 2010s–2020s guitar pop descended from Pavement, GBV, Flying Nun and Big Star: jangle, fuzz, conversational lyrics, short songs, DIY release culture.

name: Modern slowcore and hushed twang
definition: Slow tempos, quiet dynamics, sparse arrangements and country-tinged melodies; the 2010s–2020s descendants of Low, Red House Painters, Duster and Bedhead, often with pedal steel.

name: Emo-twang crossovers
definition: Bands from the emo and DIY punk circuit who folded country guitar, twang and Americana structures into emotional, anthemic rock.

name: Molina and the Magnolia circle
definition: Jason Molina's projects (Songs: Ohia, Magnolia Electric Co., solo) and the Secretly Canadian / Will Johnson orbit: haunted folk that grew into Crazy Horse-scale country rock.

name: Drag City deadpan school
definition: Silver Jews, Smog/Bill Callahan, Palace/Bonnie 'Prince' Billy and their Drag City kin: flat, wry, literary vocals over sparse or shambling country-tinged rock.

name: Southern storytelling rock
definition: Drive-By Truckers and the bands around them: three-guitar Southern rock carrying novelistic, unglamorous songs about the modern South.

name: Roots-inflected 2000s indie
definition: 2000s indie rock that absorbed country, folk and Americana textures without becoming an alt-country band: Wilco after A.M., My Morning Jacket, Okkervil River, Calexico, Lambchop, Band of Horses.

name: Rootsy indie folk
definition: Late-'90s to 2010s folk songwriters and duos with old-time, bluegrass and Appalachian roots rendered in indie terms: Gillian Welch, Iron & Wine, early Fleet Foxes, Bon Iver, Angel Olsen.

name: 2000s–2010s alt-country
definition: Alt-country after the No Depression boom: Bloodshot and Lost Highway-era songwriters and bands (Neko Case, Ryan Adams, Richmond Fontaine, Lydia Loveless, Hurray for the Riff Raff).

name: Neo-traditional and 'new outlaw' country
definition: Independent country of the 2010s–2020s that reached back to outlaw, Bakersfield and honky-tonk styles: Sturgill Simpson, Tyler Childers, Margo Price, Colter Wall, Charley Crockett.

name: American Primitive and solo guitar
definition: Fingerstyle steel-string guitar from John Fahey and Takoma through Jack Rose, William Tyler, Marisa Anderson and Hayden Pedigo; instrumental Americana with drone and raga.

name: No Depression and insurgent country
definition: The 1987–1999 alt-country boom: Uncle Tupelo, the Jayhawks, Son Volt, early Wilco, Whiskeytown, Old 97's, Bloodshot's insurgent-country roster and the Gothic country wing.

name: Slacker and '90s indie rock
definition: Pavement, Archers of Loaf, Superchunk, Built to Spill, Silkworm, Polvo, early Modest Mouse: loose, off-kilter guitar rock with conversational vocals, Matador/Merge/Touch and Go culture.

name: Lo-fi and home taping
definition: Four-track and cassette culture: Guided by Voices, Sebadoh, Daniel Johnston, Elephant 6, the Microphones, early Mountain Goats; home recording treated as an aesthetic.

name: Slowcore and sadcore
definition: Galaxie 500, Low, Red House Painters, Codeine, Bedhead, Duster, American Music Club, Mazzy Star: slow tempos, quiet dynamics, sadness as method.

name: Americana songwriters before the label
definition: Songwriters who bridged country, folk and rock before 'Americana' was a format: Lucinda Williams, Steve Earle's '90s, Vic Chesnutt, Victoria Williams, Dave Alvin, Joe Henry.

name: Cowpunk and LA roots punk
definition: Punk bands who turned to country and rockabilly: X, the Blasters, the Gun Club, Rank and File, Lone Justice, Jason & the Scorchers, the Mekons' country turn.

name: Paisley Underground
definition: Early-'80s LA neo-psychedelia and roots rock: the Dream Syndicate, Green on Red, the Long Ryders, Rain Parade, Opal; Velvets and Byrds revived with punk energy.

name: American underground and college rock
definition: SST, Twin/Tone, Homestead and IRS-era bands: R.E.M., the Replacements, Hüsker Dü, Minutemen, Meat Puppets, Dinosaur Jr., Sonic Youth, Camper Van Beethoven, the Feelies.

name: Jangle and power pop, Big Star to GBV
definition: Big Star, the dB's, Let's Active, Game Theory, Guadalcanal Diary, Teenage Fanclub, Velvet Crush: ringing guitars, harmonies, hooks in the Byrds/Beatles line.

name: Flying Nun and Antipodean indie
definition: Dunedin and Australian indie: the Clean, the Chills, the Verlaines, Tall Dwarfs, the Bats, the Go-Betweens, the Triffids; homemade jangle and drone.

name: 1980s country rebels
definition: Mainstream-adjacent country that fought Nashville's gloss: Steve Earle's Guitar Town era, Dwight Yoakam, Lyle Lovett, k.d. lang, the Desert Rose Band, Rosanne Cash.

name: Neil Young and the Crazy Horse universe
definition: Buffalo Springfield, Neil Young's solo and Crazy Horse catalog, Crazy Horse's own records, CSNY: ragged electric guitar, high cracked voice, country and folk sides.

name: Country rock and Cosmic American Music
definition: The Byrds, Gram Parsons, the Flying Burrito Brothers, Emmylou Harris, Gene Clark, Dillard & Clark, Michael Nesmith, Poco: '60s rock musicians playing sincere country.

name: Dylan and The Band
definition: Bob Dylan from going electric through the Rolling Thunder era and The Band's catalog: the model for roots-conscious rock songwriting.

name: Outlaw country
definition: Waylon Jennings, Willie Nelson, Billy Joe Shaver, Kris Kristofferson, Jessi Colter, David Allan Coe, Johnny Paycheck, Bobby Bare: Nashville outsiders with rock production and songwriter values.

name: Texas songwriters and progressive country
definition: Townes Van Zandt, Guy Clark, Jerry Jeff Walker, the Flatlanders, Joe Ely, Butch Hancock, Blaze Foley, Doug Sahm: Houston, Austin and Lubbock songwriting.

name: Country-folk storytellers
definition: John Prine, Tom T. Hall, Mickey Newbury, Steve Goodman, Bobbie Gentry, Lee Hazlewood, Karen Dalton: plainspoken narrative songwriting between folk and country.

name: Honky-tonk, Bakersfield, and hard country
definition: Merle Haggard, Buck Owens, George Jones, Loretta Lynn, Tammy Wynette, Dolly Parton, Johnny Cash, Gary Stewart, Wynn Stewart: the hard-country mainstream the V keeps returning to.

name: The Grateful Dead and California country-psych
definition: Workingman's Dead, American Beauty, Jerry Garcia's solo and bluegrass sides, New Riders of the Purple Sage: the Dead's country-folk turn and its jam offshoots.

name: Southern rock and country soul
definition: The Allman Brothers, Lynyrd Skynyrd, the Marshall Tucker Band, Little Feat, Tony Joe White, Dan Penn, Muscle Shoals: Southern guitar rock and swamp soul.

name: Velvet Underground and proto-indie
definition: The Velvet Underground, Lou Reed, Nico, the Modern Lovers/Jonathan Richman: drone, deadpan and amateurism as virtues.

name: British folk rock (selective)
definition: Fairport Convention, Sandy Denny, Richard & Linda Thompson, Nick Drake, Bert Jansch: the UK strand of folk rock that indie folk keeps citing.

name: Roots
definition: Pre-1965 country, folk and bluegrass foundations: Carter Family, Jimmie Rodgers, Hank Williams, Harry Smith's Anthology, Woody Guthrie, the Louvins, the Everlys, Lefty Frizzell, Bob Wills, Sun-era Cash, Patsy Cline, Stanley Brothers, Bill Monroe.

name: Mainstream Nashville, countrypolitan to bro-country
definition: The commercial country mainstream from the Nashville Sound to bro-country and Morgan Wallen.

name: Red Dirt, Texas country, and arena Americana
definition: Oklahoma/Texas scene country and the arena-scale Americana of Chris Stapleton and Zach Bryan.

name: Big-tent Americana and stomp-clap folk
definition: Old Crow Medicine Show, the Avett Brothers, Mumford & Sons, the Lumineers, Brandi Carlile: the festival-scale Americana mainstream.

name: Bluegrass, old-time, and newgrass
definition: Alison Krauss, Nickel Creek, Punch Brothers, Billy Strings, Molly Tuttle, Sierra Ferrell: the bluegrass line as its own tradition.

name: Chamber, baroque, and freak folk
definition: Sufjan Stevens, Joanna Newsom, Devendra Banhart, Beirut, the Decemberists: ornate indie folk that leads elsewhere.

name: Emo and Midwest emo
definition: Cap'n Jazz, American Football, Modern Baseball: the emo line from which C9 borrows.

name: Heartland rock
definition: Springsteen, Petty, Mellencamp, Seger: arena-scale American rock that occasionally feeds the V (Nebraska).

name: Grunge and '90s alt radio
definition: Nirvana, Pearl Jam, Soundgarden, Mudhoney, Screaming Trees: the Seattle line and its radio aftermath.

name: Classic shoegaze and dream pop
definition: My Bloody Valentine, Slowdive, Ride, Cocteau Twins, Swirlies: the guitar-wall vocabulary countrygaze borrows.

name: Post-punk and noise rock
definition: Wire, Mission of Burma, Big Black, Fugazi, and modern post-punk like Robber Robber: the rhythmic, angular line adjacent to the scene.

name: Modern Southern rock
definition: Blackberry Smoke, Whiskey Myers: Southern rock's mainstream continuation.

name: Pop and indie artists' country turns
definition: Kacey Musgraves, Orville Peck, CMAT, Beyoncé's Cowboy Carter: country as a mode for pop and indie artists.

name: Laurel Canyon and '70s soft rock
definition: Joni Mitchell, CSN, Jackson Browne, the Eagles, Linda Ronstadt, Harry Nilsson: the LA singer-songwriter mainstream next door to country rock.

name: Punk and hardcore roots
definition: Ramones, Black Flag, Minor Threat: the punk foundation under cowpunk, SST and the DIY network.
